# fastf 3.18.0: the desk, for the one on top

Nothing about an existing project changes. Every `PROJECT_INFO.md`,
`config.toml` and template works untouched, and no command, flag or file format
was removed. A todo nobody dates or assigns is written as it always was.

This release is for whoever oversees many projects at once, now that agents
work inside them at speed: what is waiting on you, what is moving without you,
and what has gone quiet — read from the folders, never guessed.

## Todos carry their owner and their dates

A todo's line may end in a **trailer**: `@owner`, `added:<stamp>`,
`done:<stamp>`, each a plain token a person or an agent can write by hand.

```markdown
- [ ] colour grade @claude added:2026-10-12T14:02:11Z
- [x] shoot @sales added:2026-09-20T10:00:00Z done:2026-09-28T18:30:00Z
```

- `fastf todo add` stamps `added:`; `todo done` stamps `done:` and `--undo`
  takes it off; `todo edit` keeps the trailer; `todo owner <id> <n> <name>`
  (or `--none`) hands a todo over; `--owner` and `--mine` on `todo add` name
  the owner as it is written. `todo list` shows the owner and the day.
- In the pane the owner and the day sit at the row's right, and **`O` on a
  todo** picks whose court it is in: an owner the list already names, your
  hat, nobody, or a name you type.
- A template's starter todos may end in `@owner`, so a new project is born
  with its balls in their courts.
- `fastf journal --todos` interleaves every todo ticked (and `--todos=all`,
  added) with the notes, each row saying which; the JSON rows gain `kind`.
- A line without a trailer is a todo without an owner and without dates, and
  nothing backfills them: fastf does not know when a hand wrote it.

## The hat

`fastf hat sales` wears `@sales`: the owner whose court is yours. The app's
header shows it, the desk opens on your court, `todo add --mine` assigns to
it, and `FASTF_HAT` wears one for a shell without writing anything. Nothing
else reads it; the hat never changes what a file says.

## `fastf agent`

`agent = "claude"` in `config.toml` (or `fastf config set agent claude`) names
one shell line, the shape a post-create command has. `fastf agent <query>`
runs it with the project as its working folder and `FASTF_PROJECT_PATH` set,
in the terminal you are in — so you never `cd`. From a desktop launcher it
opens a terminal window running the agent; in the app, **`x`** opens a new
window per agent so the desk stays up, and **`X`** runs it here, the app
stepping aside until it exits and re-reading the pane when it comes back.
fastf keeps no registry of agents: the folder's trace is the agent's status.

## The desk

**`w` in the app, and `fastf desk` on the command line**: every project as
one line, under whose court its ball is in. The ball is the project's first
open todo; the court is its owner — `your court`, `with @claude`, `with
@acme` — a ball nobody was named for is `unowned` (the one on top's pile until
handed off), and a project with no open todo has `nothing planned`. Within a
court the stalest project comes first. Each line says how long the project
has been quiet, `active` when a program is working in it right now (Linux,
from the process table), and `⚠` when a ball has sat in an owner's court for
three days with nothing written and nobody working: the stuck agent, said in
facts. No due dates, no priorities, no lifecycle to set.

- `f` shows a court alone, `F` or Esc every court again; `s`/`S` order a
  court (quiet, recent, name, id); `z` puts the cursor on a project picked at
  random. The desk's pane is the library's pane and every project verb works
  on the row under the cursor. Esc steps back to the library; `w` too.
- The records are read once each, a base at a time, and checked against the
  disk every ten seconds while the desk is on screen, so a todo an agent
  ticks moves its project to the right court without a keypress.
- On the command line: `fastf desk --mine`, `--owner claude`, `--unowned`,
  `--nothing-planned`, `--quiet 7`, `--random`, `--order`, `--as <hat>`,
  `--json`. On a terminal it opens the app on the tab; `--plain` keeps the
  list.
- A bare `fastf` opens on the desk when it was quit there; the session
  remembers the court, the order and when the desk was last open.

## The glance

What a hand opens a folder to see, without opening it:

- **`fastf peek <query>`** prints one project's card: the ball and its court,
  the todos' standing, who is working in the folder, what last moved under
  it, the repository's head (read from `.git` as files, no `git` started),
  the last note, how long quiet.
- **The pane** gains a `glance` section ahead of the variables: `last moved`
  (the newest file under the folder, from the size scan; a dot-folder such
  as `.git` is bookkeeping and never it), `head`, and `working` (who has
  their working folder in the project, checked once a second while the pane
  shows it; Linux).
- **`L` gains a journal page**: every dated note and every todo added or
  ticked across every project, newest first, with a rule where the desk was
  last open, so what happened since you last looked reads above it.

## Smaller things

- The header keeps all three tabs down to forty columns.
- `fastf show --json` carries the todos' `owner`, `added` and `done_at`.
- The settings screen has `hat` and `agent` rows beside `editor`.

Full key list: [docs/app.md](https://github.com/cristocola/fast-folder/blob/main/docs/app.md);
